faithful.instructions: Is the statement supported in substance by the quoted directive? Evaluate the policy obligation, not literal phrasing. Ordinary formalization may replace informal language with must, describe printing/logging using stdout or stderr, and express JSON output as a JSON object when the quote does not distinguish JSON shapes. One directive may be extracted from a compound quote. A specific encryption algorithm or stronger security policy is substantive invention. Vague quoted requirements may remain vague and faithful.

faithful.instructions: Compare anchor.statement to anchor.quote for preservation of the user requirement. Treat ordinary technical representation and output-channel descriptions as formalization: JSON/object terminology and log/print/stdout/stderr terminology do not alone add a new policy unless the quote explicitly distinguishes them. Extracting one quoted duty is allowed. Introducing a named algorithm or security strength is a new policy. Ignore the statement's grammatical form, vagueness, bundling and testability.

faithful.instructions: Does anchor.quote substantively authorize the duty in anchor.statement? Read informal user language as a requirement. Allow one atomic duty from several quoted duties, technical output-channel formalization for printing or logging, and ordinary JSON container terminology where no container distinction was specified. Preserve vagueness rather than inventing precision. Reject added policy commitments, including selecting an encryption algorithm or strength absent from the quote.
